cohort: Pregnant women aged >35 years (advanced maternal age) compared to those aged 20-34 years, using data from the Hospital Production System (SIH/SUS) in Brazil from 2012 to 2022.
finding: Pregnant women with advanced maternal age showed statistically significant higher percentages of cesarean sections, low birth weight newborns, lower APGAR scores at five minutes, a higher prevalence of congenital anomalies, and a higher incidence of premature and multiple pregnancies.
mod_finding: Pregnant women with advanced maternal age had a higher percentage of cesarean sections (63.3%) compared to non-AMA women (58%).
